newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT - Indian GDR market defies expectations.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT - Indian GDR market defies expectations.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts (GDRs) continued their expectation-defying performance on Tuesday, climbing more than 1.5 percent amid ongoing enthusiasm after last week's budget, dealers said.
"The market's surprising everyone now, it's really climbing the wall of worry," said one trader, referring to how the market has climbed hardest when most people expected it to stop or turn south.
"Whenever the market takes a breath, someone comes in to buy," he said. "The locals are very bullish -- they are talking about 4,500 (on the benchmark Bombay index) in the very short term."
Another trader said he had seen strong international client buying.
"The budget was just so unexpected, and so market- friendly, it took everyone by surprise," he said. "We are seeing continued support from London, Hong Kong and the United States."
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index closed 1.31 points, or 1.71 percent higher at 77.76 points, with the premium over the local market at 15.05 percent compared with yesterday's 14.75 percent.
The Bombay Stock Exchange 30-share index ended up 73.56 points at 3,944.61.
One dealer said blue chip GDRs like BSES, State Bank of India and Reliance were among the day's best performers.
Taiwanese GDRs also put in a respectable performance despite worries over the possibility of an interest rate rise.
One dealer said it was too early in the economic cycle for Taiwan to raise rates but that market players were keeping an eye on the central bank nonetheless.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index ended up 1.85 points, 1.81 percent, at 104.01, a premium of 0.40 percent over the local market after 0.87 percent yesterday.
The Taiwan Weighted Index closed 76.12 points, or 0.97 percent higher at 7,956.57.
The Korean market meanwhile gained support from expectations of an announcement increasing the ceiling for foreign ownership of local firms to 23 percent from 20 percent now.
These hopes outweighed news of the appointment of a new prime minister and a cabinet reshuffle in the eyes of local market players, traders said.
But one said the market would show more reaction on Wednesday, when a new finance minister is named. No word on the share ownership issue is likely until the political dust settles, he added.
The Capel Korea GDR Index ended up 0.27 points, 0.46 percent, at 36.77, a premium of 36.77 percent over the local market, compared with yesterday's 34.37 percent.
The Korea Composite Index ended up 0.33 points at 679.97. -- Caroline Brothers, London newsroom +44 171 542 5887
